v.rationale: impl-1 ranks first. Both test suites pass (impl-1: 33, impl-2: 44), and each implementation has one real bug that I confirmed with a probe. impl-2's bug is a production security hole: the password reset link is built from the request's Host header, so an attacker can make the app mail reset tokens pointing to their own domain. That breaks the 'link on our site' requirement. impl-2 also has a hand-written token middleware on the whole api group that duplicates Sanctum and returns 401 to POST /api/auth/token when a stale bearer token is sent. impl-1's bug only shows when a non-admin model is built in memory without is_admin (e.g. Sanctum::actingAs on a factory user): the bool-typed policy throws, giving 500 instead of 403. It is a real failure for tests written that way, but it is harmless in production. In design, impl-1's custom user provider enforces the block in one place for session, remember-me, login and the reset broker, and it pins APP_URL. impl-2 spreads the check across four places plus a two-mode middleware. impl-2 has the better-organised tests and the cleaner factory and policy, but that does not make up for the security bug and the extra machinery.

It also checks that the order is paid before shipping. Its tests are better organized and include a real check of the rate limiter's behaviour. v.rationale: The two implementations are nearly identical: the same controllers, FormRequest rules, routes, limiter design, Pest.php change and the same unnecessary redirectGuestsTo in bootstrap/app.php. Both pass their own suites (impl-2 18 tests, impl-1 19). Both also pass my probes for padded or uppercase email, Unicode case-folding, X-Forwarded-For spoofing, 429 and 422 JSON for non-JSON clients, double revoke, and oversized device_name or array password. Both fail the same probe: revoking from a session-authenticated request returns 500 because TransientToken has no delete(). That is out of scope for a mobile API. impl-2 ranks first on small idiom points. Its limiter reads the input once and is more readable than impl-1's crammed double input() call with a redundant trim(). Its tests are slightly cleaner: spread-based helper, a plain message assertion instead of impl-1's string-building chain, and 401 asserted on every attempt in the case-folding loop. impl-1's tests are somewhat stronger in two places: the per-IP test proves the first IP is blocked, and the token test checks tokenable. The margin is very small.
